---
title: "Bioinformatics for Molecular Biology"
subtitle: "Beginner-friendly, step-by-step tutorials for analysing molecular data"
---

Welcome! This is a growing collection of **hands-on, beginner-friendly tutorials**
that introduce interested scientists and students to bioinformatics analysis of
molecular data.

The goal is simple: take someone with a biology background and little or no
command-line experience, and walk them — one small, verifiable step at a time —
toward running real analysis pipelines.

[Start with Module 01 — Environment Setup →](modules/01-setup-environment/index.qmd){.btn .btn-primary .btn-lg role="button"}

## Who this is for

- Wet-lab biologists and students moving into computational analysis
- **Windows and macOS** users who need a proper environment to run bioinformatics
  tools (we cover both — WSL/Ubuntu on Windows, and native Terminal on Mac)
- Anyone who wants clear, reproducible, copy-pasteable demos rather than dense theory

No prior programming experience is assumed. We build up from zero.

## Available modules

The modules are designed to be followed in order — each one builds on the setup
from the module before it.

| # | Module |
|---|--------|
| 01 | [Environment Setup — Windows (WSL/Ubuntu) & macOS + Conda](modules/01-setup-environment/index.qmd) |

## A little encouragement first

Learning bioinformatics can feel like being handed a foreign-language cookbook in a
kitchen you've never seen. That feeling is completely normal — everyone starts
there, and nobody is born knowing what a "conda environment" is.

Here's the honest deal these tutorials make with you:

- **We'll guide you into the process** — clearly, one small step at a time, with no
  assumed jargon.
- **You bring the effort.** These pages are a doorway, not the whole house. Real
  comfort comes from *your* practice, curiosity, and willingness to read the
  official docs when you want to go deeper.
- **Getting stuck is part of it.** An error message is not a verdict on your
  ability; it's just the next puzzle. (Seasoned bioinformaticians spend a
  surprising amount of their day googling error messages too — you're in good
  company.)

Be patient with yourself, keep practising, and you *will* get comfortable. Let's go.

## How to use these tutorials

- **Follow along by typing**, not just reading. Muscle memory matters.
- Every command block can be copied with the button in its top-right corner.
- Each module opens with a **gentle introduction** — what the topic is, why it
  matters, and what to expect — before any commands.
- Look for the callout boxes:
  - ✅ **Check** — how to confirm a step actually worked
  - ⚠️ **Verify** — something that changes over time; confirm against current docs
  - 🧰 **Troubleshooting** — common errors and fixes

::: {.callout-important}
## A note on accuracy

Bioinformatics tooling changes fast. Tool versions, command flags, package APIs,
and even installation methods are updated regularly and some may have changed
since these tutorials were written. **Treat every version number as an example**,
pin versions in your own environments, and verify commands against the current
official documentation for each tool. Where something is known to change often,
you'll see a ⚠️ **Verify** callout.
:::
